observations: Bare engine block photographed sitting directly on dirt/gravel ground, not on a stand or pallet.
Valve cover carries 'TSI' lettering and a Volkswagen (VW) roundel badge, visible in photo 0, 1 and 2.
Intake piping, sensors, wiring harness stubs, and various hoses are attached and hanging loose.
A metal bracket near a cylindrical housing in photo 0 may be a turbo/manifold assembly, but it is not clearly resolved.
No transmission/bellhousing, starter, alternator, or accessory belt system is visible in any photo.
No engine code sticker, ID plate, or VIN tag is legible in any photo.
No oil dipstick level, coolant, or any video/sound of the engine running is shown.
Dirt and surface grime coat the block; no close-up of the casting or connector pins to judge corrosion or impact damage.

claims.evidence: VW and TSI markings are visible on the valve cover in photos 0-2, but no shot shows the full engine including turbo, manifolds, starter, alternator, or bellhousing to confirm 'complete'.

risks.risk: Engine may not be truly complete (missing turbo, manifolds, starter, alternator, or sensors).
risks.proof: Full 360° photos of the engine including intake manifold, exhaust manifold/turbo, starter motor, alternator, and bellhousing face.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an incomplete long block, missing major bolt-on components

risks.risk: Exact 1.4 TSI variant unknown (twincharger supercharged+turbo vs single-turbo, power output), which changes value significantly.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code sticker/plate, usually on the block near the oil filter housing or on a sticker on the cam cover.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lower-value single-turbo variant

risks.risk: Running condition is unverified; engine could be seized, knocking, or have internal damage.
risks.proof: Video of the engine cranking/running with audible sound, no smoke, and oil pressure light off.

risks.risk: Unknown mileage/history; could be high-mileage or from a flood/accident-damaged donor vehicle.
risks.proof: Photo of donor vehicle's odometer or any paperwork/import documentation for the engine.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown/high-mileage with no history

risks.risk: Surface corrosion or hidden damage under the dirt coating on the block could indicate poor storage or external damage.
risks.proof: Clean, well-lit close-up photos of the bare block casting and connector pins.

proof_requests: Close-up of the engine code/ID sticker or stamped code on the block.
Video of the engine cranking or running with sound.
Photos showing all sides of the engine, including turbo, manifolds, starter, alternator, and bellhousing.
Any paperwork, odometer photo, or import history from the donor vehicle.
response.reason: The engine is identifiable by type and brand (VW 1.4 TSI) from visible badging, but completeness, exact variant, and running condition are all unverified, so it must be priced at the worst case as a bare, non-running, possibly incomplete long block.
